# Naming: training sets and models have separate version numbers

A training **set** and a **model** each have their own version counter. The number in a set's name says nothing about
the number in a model's name: "train v4 from v3 data" is a model version 4 trained on set 3. Both are written with a
leading `v`, so **always say which one you mean**: "set v3", "model v4.3", in chat, logs, commit messages and UI text.

| Thing | Name | Examples | Sidecar |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| Training set | `v<SET>` or `v<SET>.<REVISION>` | `v2`, `v2.1` | `training_set.json` in the set's folder |
| Model | `v<VERSION>.<EPOCH>`, file stem may lead with `label-` | `v4.3`, `sem-v1.5` | `<stem>.model.json` beside the weights |

## Training sets: `v#` / `v#.#`

- `v2` is a set made by one exporter recipe. `v2.1` is a repopulated or tweaked `v2`: **the same creation rules**, new
  contents (a re-export after annotation edits, an updated ignore list, a corrected crop). A change to the creation
  rules (crop size, diameter handling, filtering, what counts as a sample) is a new set number, `v3`, not `v2.2`.
- A published set is immutable. Never overwrite `v2` in place: make `v2.1`.
- Revisions compare numerically: `v2` < `v2.1` < `v2.2` < `v2.10` < `v3`.
- The `current` symlink is a pointer, not a version. Anything that records a set stores the resolved folder name
  (`data_record.py` already does: `set` is the realpath's basename, `requested` is `current`).
- Every set is generated with a sidecar, **`training_set.json`, in each volume's folder** (for example
  `Y:\SAM2TrainingData\TEM\v2.1\RC1\training_set.json`). Nornir's `ExportTrainingData` writes it into its `-Output` folder
  (`-SetVersion v2.1`, optional `-ParentSet`, `-SetDescription`), and `version-sync` copies the folder, so it travels with
  the volume's data. Fields: `schema_version`, `set_version` (equals the set's folder name), `parent` (`v2` for `v2.1`,
  null for a new set), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `generator` (tool and version), `creation_rules` (the exporter
  parameters that define a sample), `creation_rules_fingerprint` (hash of `creation_rules`: **equal across a set and its
  revisions**, different across set numbers), `source` (the annotation source, not a rule), and `description` (free text
  an operator may edit; a re-export keeps it). The exporter refuses to export under a set number whose rules have
  changed. See Nornir's `Training-set-naming` rule.
- The trainer's `training_data.json` (the run's record of what it saw) names the set the same way; its `set` field is
  this folder name.

## Models: `v<VERSION>.<EPOCH>`

- `VERSION` is the model's own counter (the `4` in run `sam2_em_v4`). `EPOCH` is the trainer's epoch index as printed in
  the log and used in `checkpoint_epoch<N>.pt` and `serve_epoch<N>.pt`; it starts at 0, so `v4.0` is the model after
  the first epoch. State the base when it matters.
- The weights file stem ends with the model name: `v4.3.pt` with `v4.3.model.json` beside it. A dot in the stem is
  fine (`model_manifest.manifest_path` appends `.model.json` to `Path.stem`).
- The stem may lead with labels joined to the name by `-`, for example `sem-v1.5.pt` (modality) or `tem-gpu-v4.3.pt`:
  `[<label>-]...v<VERSION>.<EPOCH>`, labels made of letters, digits and `_`. The labels are for people sorting files;
  the sidecars follow the whole stem (`sem-v1.5.model.json`, `sem-v1.5.prompt_encoding.json`), and the model name
  inside them stays unlabelled. A stem that ends in a different version than the model's (`sem-v1.4.pt` holding epoch
  5) is an error: the exporter refuses it and `model_manifest check` reports it.
- The manifest's `model.model_version` is `v<VERSION>.<EPOCH>` and `model.model_id` is `v<VERSION>`; neither takes a
  label. The server's per-model host name follows the id (`v4.segmentation.codepharm.net`) and clients send
  `model_id` with requests.
- The sidecar `<stem>.model.json` (`docs/model_manifest.md`) carries a **`description`** field the operator fills in to
  say what the model is (what changed, what to use it for). The operator's source is **<run>/model.json** (model_id,
  display_name, description); the exporter writes it with inferred defaults the first time and never overwrites it, and
  an export never overwrites a description already in a sidecar. Precedence: argument, model.json, existing sidecar, inferred.
- The model sidecar records the training set separately (`training_data.set`, a set name as above) and never
  derives one number from the other.

## Existing names stay as they are

Do not rename old files. `v1`, `v1b` (a letter suffix is legacy; do not create new ones), `v3` sets and weights such as
`sam2_em_v3_epoch_9.pt` or `v2_epoch_8.pt` keep their names; give them a hand-written manifest whose `model_version`
follows the convention (`v3.9`, `v2.8`).

## Where this is implemented

- Set names: `scripts/WSL/training_data_common.sh` (`version_name_ok`, `version_sort_key`: `v#`, `v#.#`, the old `v1b`,
  numeric order), tested by `tests/test_training_data_versions.py`.
- Model names and `description`: `model_manifest.py` (validates `v<VERSION>` / `v<VERSION>.<EPOCH>`; `MODEL_STEM_RE`,
  `stem_model_version`, `stem_mismatch` for the optional `label-` prefix on file stems) and
  `export_serve.py` (`--model-id`, `--epoch`, `--display-name`, `--description`; reads/writes `<run>/model.json`; keeps an
  existing description; refuses before loading weights when the version or epoch is unknown, or when `--out` is named for
  another version). Training writes `best_model.json` (the epoch of `best_model.pt`) so a
  hand export can name it. The Viking server passes `description` on in `ModelInfo`.
- Set sidecar: Nornir's `training_set.py` (`CheckTrainingSet` first, `WriteTrainingSetInfo` last in `ExportTrainingData`).

## Status: not done yet

Delete an item when it is done.

- `scripts/NAS/version-bump` and `version-sync` do not check that a volume's `training_set.json` `set_version` equals
  the set folder they copy it into, or that a revision's `creation_rules_fingerprint` matches its parent's.
- The trainer's `training_data.json` and the model manifest's `training_data` block do not read each volume's
  `training_set.json` yet (they fingerprint the manifest, approved and ignore files themselves). Carrying the set's
  `set_version`, `creation_rules_fingerprint` and `description` into them would make the lineage visible to clients.
